title: Navimower 0.4.3

## Highlights

Navimower 0.4.3 is the cumulative stable release of the 0.4.3 beta line. It is built on 0.4.2 and already contains all beta1-beta59 changes; no beta release needs to be installed first.

### Navimower Schedule

- Adds the integration-owned **Navimower Schedule** for one-zone-at-a-time mowing with **Automatic** oldest-completed order or a persistent **Custom** queue.
- Supports **Time window** and **24 hours** modes. Time-window closing sends the mower Home/Dock while retaining the unfinished task so reopening can resume it without creating a new mowing cycle.
- Schedule Off/On is reversible pause/resume of scheduler ownership and progress. It preserves the current round, Custom queue position, active-zone ownership and retained interruption state.
- Adds **Reset schedule progress** as a normal Home Assistant device Control and the matching `navimower.reset_schedule` action for intentional destructive reset of the current scheduler round. Reset sends no mower command and is refused while the mower is mowing or returning.
- Completion is based on trustworthy fresh per-zone completion evidence, not docking, stale progress, route progress or whole-task percentage alone.
- Supports direct handoff to the next queued zone after confirmed completion when the mower is in a normal return transition; low-battery charging returns remain mower-owned.
- Charging recovery waits for mower self-resume first, uses the configured charging limit only as a fallback threshold, re-checks the Time window before any fallback Resume and never converts an interrupted task into `reset=true`.
- Native Navimow Schedule and Navimower Schedule remain mutually exclusive.

### Map, zones and mowing history

- Adds stable per-zone **Coverage**, **Area**, **Mowed area**, **Last mowed** and conservative **Last completed** entities backed by the integration zone model.
- Separates physical mower zone, task target zone, active-zone progress and whole-task progress so transit through another polygon cannot incorrectly transfer task ownership or completion.
- Uses fresh current-cycle vendor per-zone coverage reaching 100% as the final authority for `Last completed`.
- Adds reset-based **current-cycle history**: a confirmed new cycle replaces only the zone that starts the new cycle, while pause/resume, charging continuation and `reset=false` splits stay accumulated in the same cycle.
- Current-cycle trails persist across midnight until a confirmed new cycle starts for that zone.
- Adds backend `current_cycle_render` to the authenticated Map API. Completed current-cycle mowing swaths are rendered and cached by Home Assistant instead of being rebuilt in every browser; the active live trail remains separate.
- Watches vendor `mapVersion` so map edits invalidate stale geometry and refresh map/location data promptly.
- Removes stale zone sensor registry rows after a freshly decoded, versioned map proves that old vendor zone IDs no longer exist. Historical sessions are preserved.

### Custom Areas and gate automation

- Adds persistent **Custom Areas** imported from a temporary Navimow Off-limit polygon and stored locally by Navimower.
- Custom Areas are independent of the later mowing-zone layout and can be used for virtual presence areas such as gate passages, driveways or narrow corridors.
- Custom Area occupancy uses fresh official MQTT X/Y only and becomes unavailable when live pose is stale or missing; it does not present a stale private-cloud coordinate as fresh presence.
- Documents the Navimow Off-limit limitation for Custom Areas spanning separate mowing zones: temporarily merge the required zones, capture/import the Custom Area, then restore the original zones.
- Adds a tested **Gate required + Custom Area** sliding-gate automation guide. The documented pattern is intended for Navimower Schedule or manually started single-zone mowing where the target zone is unambiguous, with the Custom Area extending slightly into the mowing zone before the physical gate.
- Gate/navigation fallback prefers MQTT but can use sufficiently fresh private-cloud local position conservatively. Risky cloud-only gate clear/close transitions require repeated vendor position evidence.

### Position, state and telemetry

- Adds a native Home Assistant **Location** `device_tracker` when the private cloud reports valid latitude/longitude. Dense MQTT X/Y remains mower-local Cartesian map data.
- Keeps MQTT connection health separate from live-position validity and exposes position source/age and stream health explicitly.
- Improves private-cloud/MQTT state arbitration, problem latching and error detail handling. Private `error_data` remains the canonical active numeric fault source while MQTT error-state edges can request a fast canonical refresh.
- A confirmed docked/charging mower is shown in the virtual **Dock** physical area instead of retaining a stale lawn-zone position.
- Stabilizes battery, task progress and task/mowed-area source selection with freshness-aware fallbacks and retained last-good values.

### Setup, multi-mower and regional routing

- Keeps one Home Assistant config entry per mower while allowing multiple mower entries to reuse the same dedicated private-cloud account identity safely.
- Initial setup now automatically selects the mower when exactly one unconfigured mower remains; the picker is shown only when two or more genuine choices remain. Manual serial fallback remains available for shared accounts whose mower is not returned by the private auth list.
- Official Smart Home OAuth mower matching remains serial/device-aware so the private-cloud and official branches resolve to the same mower.
- Extends private-cloud regional handling across the observed EU/FRA, SEA/SG, US/ORE and CN/BJ families while keeping official Smart Home OAuth/MQTT routing independent.
- Preserves the raw Passport region when the mower-cloud login contract requires it; this fixes the observed US/Oregon account path where `/user/user/login` expects `ore` rather than the canonical routing alias.

### Model-aware settings and controls

- Expands capability-driven settings for modern mower families, including observed i2 AWD controls and vendor-reported limits/options where available.
- Adds/normalizes controls for mowing, positioning, terrain, weather, battery, lighting and supported model-specific features without inventing capabilities for models that do not report them.
- Standardizes the default Home Assistant display names for weather-adaptive settings, including **Frost detection**, **Frost delay**, **Rain forecast**, **Rain forecast sensitivity**, **Rain delay**, **Rain delay duration**, **Snow detection**, **Snow delay**, **Max temp detection**, **Max temperature**, **Wind detection**, and **Do not disturb start/end**. Entity keys, unique IDs and vendor read/write mappings remain unchanged.

### Notifications and diagnostics

- Keeps the merged **Latest notification** timeline with vendor and Navimower-local origins and origin-aware mark-read actions.
- Uses neutral wording for mowing starts when this Home Assistant instance cannot prove the command source and avoids duplicating the vendor low-battery return notification with a second local charging-pause row.
- Home Assistant **Download diagnostics** is cached-only, sanitized and read-only. It performs no hidden mower command, notification mutation or retired H5 discovery request.
- Optional **Passive protocol discovery** remains a separate, disabled-by-default Options Flow tool for short controlled investigations.

### Documentation and Map Card compatibility

- Rewrites the README around current setup and Options Flow behavior, including Navimower Schedule, Custom Areas, gates, current-cycle rendering, regional routing and diagnostics.
- Adds current multi-mower and tested gate-automation guides under `docs/`.
- **Navimower Map Card 0.3.5 requires Navimower integration 0.4.3 or newer.**

### Compatibility

- Existing Navimower config entries, device/entity unique IDs, map/history/session storage and notification storage are retained unless a stale zone ID has been authoritatively removed from the current map.
- Upgrading from 0.4.2 or any 0.4.3 beta does not require recreating the integration.
- No 0.4.3 beta needs to be installed before this stable release.
